rows.stem: The growth of the pollen tubes towards ovules is an example of :

options.label: A
options.text: Phototropism

options.label: B
options.text: Hydrotropism

options.label: C
options.text: Geotropism

options.label: D
options.text: Chemotropism

rows.solution:
The ovule releases chemicals, and the pollen tube grows towards it in response. A growth movement in response to a chemical stimulus is chemotropism.

This is option (D) Chemotropism.

rows.stem: Parasitic mode of nutrition is observed in :

options.label: A
options.text: *Bryophyllum*

options.label: B
options.text: *Hibiscus*

options.label: C
options.text: *Cuscuta*

options.label: D
options.text: *Helianthus*

rows.solution:
*Cuscuta* (amar-bel) is a parasitic plant: it grows on a host plant and draws its food from it without killing it. *Bryophyllum*, *Hibiscus* and *Helianthus* are green plants that make their own food.

This is option (C) *Cuscuta*.

rows.stem: A candle flame is placed in front of the reflecting surface of a convex mirror of focal length f. If the distance of the flame from the pole of the mirror is ‘f’, its image is formed :

options.label: A
options.text: at infinite distance from the mirror

options.label: B
options.text: behind the mirror at the principal focus

options.label: C
options.text: behind the mirror at a distance 2f

options.label: D
options.text: behind the mirror at a distance \(\frac{f}{2}\)

rows.solution:
For a convex mirror the focal length is positive, \(+f\), and the object distance is \(u = -f\). By the mirror formula,

\(\dfrac{1}{v} = \dfrac{1}{f} - \dfrac{1}{u} = \dfrac{1}{f} + \dfrac{1}{f} = \dfrac{2}{f}\), so \(v = +\dfrac{f}{2}\).

The image is virtual, behind the mirror, at a distance \(\dfrac{f}{2}\) from the pole.

This is option (D) behind the mirror at a distance \(\frac{f}{2}\).

rows.chapter: The Human Eye and the Colourful World
rows.stem: Select the correct statement from the following :

options.label: A
options.text: The size of the molecules of air is larger than the wavelength of visible light.

options.label: B
options.text: The blue light has a wavelength about \(1{\cdot}8\) times greater than that of red light.

options.label: C
options.text: When sunlight passes through the fine particles in air, they scatter the blue colour of visible light more strongly than red.

options.label: D
options.text: The light of red colour is scattered the most by fog or smoke.

rows.solution:
When sunlight passes through the fine particles in air, the blue end of the spectrum is scattered more strongly than red. This is why the clear sky looks blue.

The other statements are wrong: air molecules are smaller than the wavelength of visible light; it is red light whose wavelength is about \(1{\cdot}8\) times that of blue; and the large particles of fog or smoke scatter all colours about equally, so they look white.

This is option (C) When sunlight passes through the fine particles in air, they scatter the blue colour of visible light more strongly than red.

rows.stem: In domestic electric circuits, the colour of insulation covers of wires in the cables of electric iron/electric toaster is generally :

options.label: A
options.text: red for live wire, green for neutral wire and black for earth wire

options.label: B
options.text: red for live wire, black for neutral wire and green for earth wire

options.label: C
options.text: green for live wire, black for neutral wire and red for earth wire

options.label: D
options.text: green for live wire, red for neutral wire and black for earth wire

rows.solution:
In domestic wiring, the live wire has red insulation, the neutral wire black and the earth wire green.

This is option (B) red for live wire, black for neutral wire and green for earth wire.

rows.stem:
**Assertion (A) :** Brass is prepared by first melting copper and then dissolving tin into it in a definite proportion.

**Reason (R) :** The primary metal of brass is copper.
rows.context: For Questions number 17 to 20, two statements are given — one labelled as Assertion (A) and the other labelled as Reason (R). Select the correct answer to these questions from the codes (A), (B), (C) and (D) as given below.

options.label: A
options.text: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).

options.label: B
options.text: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is **not** the correct explanation of Assertion (A).

options.label: C
options.text: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.

options.label: D
options.text: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.

rows.solution:
Brass is an alloy of copper and zinc. It is made by melting copper and dissolving zinc in it in a definite proportion. Copper with tin gives bronze, not brass, so the Assertion is false.

Copper is the primary metal of brass, so the Reason is true.

The Assertion is false while the Reason is true, which is option (D).

rows.subtopic: Common Salt and Chemicals from It
rows.stem: A chemical compound ‘X’ is used to bleach washed clothes in laundry as well as to make drinking water free from germs. Identify ‘X’. How is this compound represented ? Write the method of its preparation along with the chemical equation for the reaction that occurs.
rows.solution:
X is bleaching powder (calcium oxychloride), represented as \(\mathrm{CaOCl_2}\).

It is prepared by the action of chlorine gas on dry slaked lime:

\(\mathrm{Ca(OH)_2 + Cl_2 \rightarrow CaOCl_2 + H_2O}\)

(The chlorine comes from the chlor-alkali process, the electrolysis of brine.)

rows.stem: “Sex of the children is determined by type of sex chromosome which they inherit from their father.” Justify the statement.
rows.solution:
A woman has two X chromosomes (XX), so every egg carries an X chromosome. A man has one X and one Y chromosome (XY), so half his sperms carry X and half carry Y.

If a sperm carrying X fertilises the egg, the child is XX, a girl. If a sperm carrying Y fertilises the egg, the child is XY, a boy.

The mother always gives an X, so the sex of the child depends only on whether the father gives an X or a Y chromosome. This justifies the statement.

rows.stem: Four resistors, each of resistance \(2{\cdot}0\,\Omega\), are joined end to end to form a square ABCD as shown. Using appropriate formula, determine the equivalent resistance of the combination between its two ends A and B.
rows.figureNote: REQUIRED - the stem says the square is 'as shown': a square circuit with corners A (top left), B (top right), C (bottom right) and D (bottom left), one resistor labelled 2.0 Ω on each of the four sides AB, BC, CD and DA, so A and B are adjacent corners joined directly by one resistor. Page idx 14.
rows.solution:
Between A and B there are two paths. One is the single resistor AB, \(R_1 = 2{\cdot}0\,\Omega\). The other is the three resistors AD, DC and CB in series:

\(R_s = 2 + 2 + 2 = 6\,\Omega\)

These two paths are in parallel:

\(\dfrac{1}{R_p} = \dfrac{1}{R_1} + \dfrac{1}{R_s} = \dfrac{1}{2} + \dfrac{1}{6} = \dfrac{4}{6}\), so \(R_p = \dfrac{6}{4} = 1{\cdot}5\,\Omega\).

The equivalent resistance between A and B is \(1{\cdot}5\,\Omega\).

rows.stem: State the change that is observed when a China dish containing copper powder is heated over the flame of a burner. Name the phenomenon responsible for the change and write balanced equation for the chemical reaction that occurs. How is this reaction different from the reaction that occurs when copper wares kept in open air slowly lose their shiny brown surface and gain a coat ? Write chemical name of the coating and state its colour.
rows.solution:
The reddish-brown copper powder turns black, because a layer of copper(II) oxide forms on its surface.

The phenomenon is oxidation: copper gains oxygen.

\(\mathrm{2Cu + O_2 \xrightarrow{\text{heat}} 2CuO}\)

Heating gives a quick oxidation at high temperature. The dull coat on copper wares kept in open air comes from corrosion: copper slowly reacts with moist carbon dioxide (and oxygen) in the air at ordinary temperature over a long time.

The coating is basic copper carbonate, \(\mathrm{CuCO_3 \cdot Cu(OH)_2}\), and it is green.

rows.stem: Why is blood circulation in vertebrates known as “double circulation”? Trace its path in the form of a flow chart.
rows.solution:
It is called double circulation because the blood passes through the heart twice in each complete round of the body: once on its way to and from the lungs, and once on its way to and from the rest of the body. This keeps oxygenated and deoxygenated blood separate.

Flow chart:

Lungs \(\rightarrow\) Pulmonary vein \(\rightarrow\) Left atrium \(\rightarrow\) Left ventricle \(\rightarrow\) Aorta \(\rightarrow\) Body parts (oxygenated blood)

Body parts \(\rightarrow\) Veins \(\rightarrow\) Vena cava \(\rightarrow\) Right atrium \(\rightarrow\) Right ventricle \(\rightarrow\) Pulmonary artery \(\rightarrow\) Lungs (deoxygenated blood)

(The marking scheme's chart goes straight from the right ventricle to the lungs; the pulmonary artery carries the blood between them.)

rows.chapter: The Human Eye and the Colourful World
rows.subtopic: Defects of Vision and their Correction
rows.stem: A person is suffering from an eye defect in which the far point of the eye is much nearer than infinity. Name the defect of vision the person is suffering from. List two main causes of this defect. Write the type of the corrective lens and draw a ray diagram to show the function of the corrective lens.
rows.solution:
The far point is much nearer than infinity, so the person cannot see distant objects clearly. The defect is myopia (short-sightedness).

Two causes: (i) excessive curvature of the eye lens; (ii) elongation of the eyeball.

It is corrected with a concave (diverging) lens of suitable power.

Ray diagram: draw the eye with a concave lens in front of it. Parallel rays from a distant object fall on the concave lens and diverge, so that they appear to come from the far point O of the myopic eye (shown by dotted lines produced back to O). The eye lens then focuses these rays on the retina. Label the concave lens, the retina and O, and draw arrows on the rays.

rows.stem:
(a) Name and state the rule which determines the force on a current carrying conductor placed in a uniform magnetic field.

(b) Consider the following three diagrams in which the entry of a positive charge (+Q) in a magnetic field is shown. Identify giving reason the case in which the force experienced by the charge is (i) maximum, and (ii) minimum.
rows.figureNote: REQUIRED - (b) is answered from three printed diagrams I, II and III, each showing three parallel horizontal arrows labelled 'Magnetic field' and a charge +Q entering the field with an arrow marking its direction of motion. The angle each +Q arrow makes with the field is the discriminator and is withheld here because it is the answer. (a) needs no figure. Page idx 16.
rows.solution:
(a) Fleming's left-hand rule: stretch the thumb, forefinger and middle finger of your left hand so that they are mutually perpendicular. If the forefinger points in the direction of the magnetic field and the middle finger in the direction of the current, then the thumb points in the direction of the force on the conductor.

(b) A moving positive charge is a current in its direction of motion. The force on it is greatest when it moves perpendicular to the field and zero when it moves along the field.

(i) Maximum in Case III: the charge moves perpendicular to the magnetic field.

(ii) Minimum in Case I: the charge moves parallel to the magnetic field, so it experiences no force at all. (In Case II it moves at an angle to the field, so the force lies between these.)
